Zoom, like a lot of the Oblivion / Gamebyro engine was weird. The camera actually moved closer to the subject but the drawing of objects / npcs's as well as LOD were all calculated from the players feet, so you could end up with something visible just moving into the invisible / no draw range or even clips though low detail versions of the terrain off in the distance. Thats also why a lot of the map in Fallout 3 and NV was almost all hills, small valleys and canyons. The only places you'd have a really long view distance had hills and valleys in between the things you could see far in the distance to hid the transition from low detail distant terrain / objects and higher detail nearby terrain as you travel towards something in the distance. The engine made for Skyrim / Fallout4 does a better job managing this but use the exact same tricks only way more granular (in Fallout4 anyway).
